A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BayesG research work. All 27 pages of each version, including Appendices A–I, were readable and rendered successfully, supporting comparison of text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v4 reports original traffic-control simulation results across five environments, including training rewards, ablations, and qualitative case studies in Section 5 and Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v5 retains the original simulation results across five traffic-control environments, together with the ablations, training-loss analyses, and case studies.

M1.justification: The graph-conditioned policy, variational edge masks, ELBO objective, actor–critic architecture, and training/execution procedures in Section 4 and Appendix D are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ATSC_Grid, Monaco, NewYork33, NewYork51, and NewYork167. The environments, task requirements, and appendix simulation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain IA2C, ConseNet, FPrint, LToS, CommNet, and NeurComm, with unchanged participation in the corresponding comparisons. The two newly cited works are background references, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported control intervals, episode lengths, observation/action definitions, rewards, and experimental procedures in Section 5.1 and Appendices B–D are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the masking-strategy and mask-input ablations in Figure 5, the training-loss analysis in Appendix E, and the traffic and interaction-graph case studies in Appendices F–G.

E5.justification: Both report averaging experiments over five random seeds and display the same shaded reward curves and five-run loss plots. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The reward curves, ablation results, loss trajectories, congestion snapshots, interaction-graph examples, and Table 1 graph statistics are unchanged. No result entries, numerical values, or reported findings were added or revised.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–5, the mathematical objectives and assumptions, and the detailed graph-policy and ELBO derivations in Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about decentralized Bayesian graph inference, adaptive communication, performance, and scalability to 167 agents.

C2.justification: Interpretations of adaptive coordination and training dynamics are unchanged. Appendix I retains the same limitations concerning fixed topology, local observability, hyperparameter sensitivity, and computational cost; only citation numbers change.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, environment processing details, graph statistics, and pseudocode are unchanged. The Section 5.1 code-and-data availability statement also remains identical.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Duan et al., Negative samples-enhanced graph convolutional neural networks (2021), and Yao et al., Mecon: A gnn-based graph classification framework for MEV activity detection (2025). These become references [31] and [34] in v5, expanding the bibliography from 49 to 51 works without changing the surrounding research-positioning argument.

P1.justification: Citation and reference numbering is updated throughout the main text and appendices, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Apart from the added bibliography entries, prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added references cause bibliography reflow on pages 13–14, moving two existing entries onto page 14. All eleven figures and both tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v5 adds two references to an unchanged GNN-background sentence and adjusts citation numbering and bibliography layout. The method, theoretical reasoning, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, yielding no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
